issues.legal_issue: A specific testamentary authorization to sell estate property for a stated purpose does not, without clear language restricting other dispositions, prevent an executrix from leasing property in the course of administration.
material_facts: The testator appointed his widow as executrix, gave her a life interest in the estate, and gave his son a vested remainder.
The will authorized the executrix to sell estate property to meet specified marriage expenses, directed her to pay maintenance and debts, and contained no express restriction on leasing.
The executrix granted a lease over part of the estate, and the lessee’s interest later passed to a defendant.
The claimants sought recovery of possession in a property suit, challenging the executrix’s authority to grant the lease.
The Court assumed, without finding it established, that the lease may have been granted to raise money for the specified marriage expenses.
issues.conclusion: The will did not restrict the executrix’s power to lease the property in due course of administration. The lease was binding on the claimants, who could not recover possession of the leased property in the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 90(1) of the Probate and Administration Act, 1881, an executrix may deal with estate property unless the will restricts that power in clear language. A specific authorization to sell for a stated purpose does not by itself imply a prohibition on other dispositions, including a lease; the maxim expressum facit cessare tacitum does not apply. The Court followed Purna Chandra Bakshi v. Nobin Chandra Gangopadhya, which held that an express power to sell did not impliedly prohibit mortgaging property.

rule.if: appeal_in_property_possession_suit and executrix_granted_lease_during_administration and will_authorized_sale_for_specific_purpose and will_lacks_clear_restriction_on_leasing

predicates.appeal_in_property_possession_suit: The matter is an appeal in a suit seeking possession of property subject to a disputed lease.
predicates.executrix_granted_lease_during_administr: An executrix granted a lease over estate property while administering the estate.
predicates.will_authorized_sale_for_specific_purpos: The will expressly authorized the executrix to sell estate property for a stated purpose.
predicates.will_lacks_clear_restriction_on_leasing: The will contained no clear language restricting the executrix from leasing estate property.
predicates.claimants_cannot_recover_possession_unde: The claimants cannot recover possession of the leased property from a person claiming through the lease.

issues.definition: When an executrix grants a lease during administration, a specific testamentary power to sell does not prevent recovery of possession by claimants if the will contains no clear restriction on leasing.
